title: Finding MK Average
statement:
Design a class `MKAverage` that watches a stream of integers and reports an "MK average" of its most recent part, using two fixed integers `m` and `k`.

- `MKAverage(m, k)` starts with an empty stream and stores `m` and `k`.
- `addElement(num)` appends `num` to the end of the stream.
- `calculateMKAverage()` returns `-1` while the stream holds fewer than `m` numbers. Otherwise it looks only at the `m` most recently added numbers, sets aside the `k` smallest and the `k` largest of them (duplicates count individually), and returns the mean of the `m - 2k` numbers left, rounded down to an integer.
constraints: At most 10^5 calls in total to addElement and calculateMKAverage
notes:
## Intuition

Sorting the last `m` numbers on every query costs O(m log m) per call. Notice that the middle sum is "sum of the smallest `m - k`" minus "sum of the smallest `k`". Values are at most 10⁵, so the window can live in two Fenwick trees indexed by value — one counting how many copies of each value are in the window, one summing them. Then "sum of the smallest `t`" is a single descent through the tree, like finding the `t`-th order statistic in an ordered set.

## Approach

1. Keep the stream in an array with a `head` index, so the window is `stream[head..]`.
2. `update(value, delta)` adds `delta` copies of `value` to `count` and `delta * value` to `total` along the Fenwick path.
3. `addElement` appends `num` and inserts it; if the window now holds more than `m` numbers, it removes `stream[head]` and advances `head`.
4. `sumOfSmallest(t)` descends with power-of-two `step`s, absorbing every block whose count keeps `taken` below `t`. It stops at `position`, so the remaining `t - taken` numbers all equal `position + 1`.
5. `calculateMKAverage` returns `-1` for a short window; otherwise it takes `sumOfSmallest(m - k) - sumOfSmallest(k)` and floors its mean over `m - 2k`.

## Example 1, step by step

With `m = 3`, `k = 1`: after adding 3 and 1 the window has 2 numbers, so the answer is `-1`. Adding 10 makes the window `{1, 3, 10}`; `sumOfSmallest(2) = 4`, `sumOfSmallest(1) = 1`, so the answer is `3 / 1 = 3`. Three more 5s push out 3, 1 and 10; the window is `{5, 5, 5}` and the answer is `(10 - 5) / 1 = 5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log V) per call with V = 10⁵: each update and each descent walks at most 17 levels.
- Space: O(V + n) for the two trees and the stored stream.

## Pitfalls

- Duplicates matter: the `k` smallest may include several copies of one value, which the "`t - taken` copies of `position + 1`" step handles.
- Remove the oldest number from the trees as soon as the window exceeds `m`, not only when a query arrives.
- Floor the mean; sums reach 10¹⁰, still exact in a JavaScript number.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count`, `total` | Fenwick trees of copies and sums per value range |
| `stream`, `head` | every added number; the window starts at `head` |
| `position` | largest value whose prefix holds fewer than `t` numbers |
| `taken`, `sum` | numbers and their sum absorbed so far in the descent |
| `middle` | sum of the window after dropping `k` from each end |
